item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Aaron Judge is on the injured list again, but the Yankees could get two key pieces back off of it by next week.
Jazz Chisholm Jr. should be activated on the upcoming homestand that begins Tuesday, Aaron Boone said Friday, after the second baseman landed on the IL last week with a right thumb sprain.




Access the Yankees beat like never before


Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
Try it free
Friday marked his fourth day of hitting in a row after being shut down from baseball activities for about a week, while he has also been throwing the last couple of days.
“He’s getting very close,” Boone said before the Yankees’ 9-2 win over the Diamondbacks at Chase Field.
Trent Grisham, meanwhile, is “pretty far into his running progression” from a right hamstring strain and “doing well,” Boone said, putting him in position to be in play at the end of the regular season.
Before Judge’s calf strain, it was questionable whether there would be a lane for Grisham to get playing time if and when he returned.
But now it is possible he could return to center field at least against righties, bumping Spencer Jones to right field.
As for Ryan Weathers, the other Yankee trying to make it back in time for the playoffs (from a left forearm flexor strain), Boone acknowledged the lefty is “unlikely to get into a game before the end of the season.”
Weathers is set to throw a second bullpen session on Saturday, after which he could advance to facing hitters in live batting practice.
Whether that will give him enough time to show he should be part of the bullpen for the first round of the playoffs remains to be seen.
“We’ll see what our needs are and how he looks and if we feel like he’s ready to come in and be a contributor,” Boone said.
Anthony Volpe, who was back at second base, hit .348 with a .965 OPS and four steals in his first seven games since being called back up from Triple-A as an injury replacement for Chisholm.
He was 0-for-4 in Friday night’s win.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX - Gerrit Cole nunca había permitido siete jonrones en un lapso de dos aperturas antes de sus salidas más recientes y, con los playoffs a la vuelta de la esquina, existía la preocupación de que el lanzador derecho de los Yankees hubiera sufrido un bajón de rendimiento.
La mayor parte de esa inquietud provenía de fuera del vestuario. El manager de los Yankees, Aaron Boone, afirmó el viernes que se esperaba que Cole abriera un partido si su equipo llegaba a la Serie de Comodines de la Liga Americana, y el veterano cumplió su promesa de solucionar el problema de los cuadrangulares y lanzó bien en la victoria por 9-2 sobre los Diamondbacks en el Chase Field el viernes por la noche.
Los Yankees (89-64) ganaron por 11ma vez en 15 partidos, colocándose a cuatro juegos de los Rays en la División Este de la Liga Americana después de que Tampa Bay perdiera ante Boston más temprano esa misma noche.
Horas después de que Cody Bellinger dijera que los Yankees tendrían que "apoyarse mutuamente" para superar la ausencia de Aaron Judge —quien, tras ganar tres veces el premio al Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana, podría perderse el resto de la temporada regular debido a una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha—, los "Bombarderos" respaldaron a Cole con una primera entrada de cinco carreras.
Cada uno de los primeros cinco bateadores se embasó y anotó ante el venzolano Eduardo Rodríguez. Ben Rice negoció una base por bolas con las bases llenas, el dominicano Amed Rosario conectó un sencillo productor y George Lombard Jr. disparó un sencillo de dos carreras; esto fue parte de una noche de tres carreras impulsadas para el novato, quien también conectó un jonrón en la sexta entrada que provocó la salida de Rodríguez del juego.
Rice también conectó su 39no jonrón —líder del equipo— para apoyar a Cole, quien había permitido jonrones al primer bateador en sus dos aperturas anteriores. Tras dedicar tiempo a ajustar su mecánica de lanzamiento y corregir posibles problemas de revelación de pitcheos desde su última salida contra los Mets, Cole retiró a los bateadores de Arizona en orden durante una primera entrada de 12 lanzamientos.
Corbin Carroll conectó un jonrón de dos carreras ante Cole en la segunda entrada, pero eso fue todo lo que lograron los D-backs. Con un total de 90 lanzamientos (62 strikes), Cole permitió cuatro imparables, no otorgó bases por bolas y ponchó a seis bateadores.

item.title: [Pinstripe Alley] Yankees ride five-run first to series-opening romp of Diamondbacks
item.dc:creator: Peter Brody
item.description: The two starting pitchers entered this game trending in opposite directions. item.content:encoded:
The two starting pitchers entered this game trending in opposite directions. Gerrit Cole had just allowed the most home runs (seven) in a two-start span in his career, while Eduardo Rodriguez is in the midst of a career year with a 2.62 ERA. One of those trends remained — Cole giving up another home run on a fastball — but fortunately the other trend was momentarily halted, the Yankees scoring five in the first off E-Rod to give themselves enough of a cushion to weather Cole’s continued home run woes.
Cole settled down after the Carroll dinger to give the Yankees six innings, by which time the offense all but put this game out of reach. They kept the pressure on, scoring a further four runs including solo home runs by Ben Rice and George Lombard Jr., to cruise to a series-opening victory in the desert, 9-2.
Rodriguez came into this game with an ERA above six in the first inning and an ERA right around two for the subsequent innings combined. That made it imperative that the Yankees find a way to do damage before the home team had a chance to come to bat, especially with the rate Cole is giving up the long ball. They did just that with a clear disciplined approach not to expand the zone against E-Rod’s curveball.
Paul Goldschmidt drew a leadoff walk, Cody Bellinger followed with a single, and Heliot Ramos also walked to load the bases with no outs. Rice drew the Yankees’ third walk in the first four batters to plate Goldschmidt and open the scoring, Goldy, Ramos, and Rice all working full counts before taking the free pass. Amed Rosario then fought off a cutter that handcuffed him up and in, muscling it to the opposite field perfectly between center and left fielder to plate Bellinger as the runners went station to station. A wild pitch allowed Ramos to score and Rice and Rosario to move up to second and third. This set up a two-run ground ball single from Lombard that just got by Geraldo Perdomo’s diving attempt to atone for his defensive misplay in the 13th that allowed the Twins to walk off the Yankees on Wednesday.
Rodriguez struck out Volpe to end the inning giving him three strikeouts in the frame, but the damage was done. The 45 pitches he threw were the most he’s thrown in the first inning in his career. 33 of those pitches fell out of the zone, but only eight induced a chase.
It’s a good thing they hung such a crooked number, because Cole immediately gave two of those runs back. He gave up a leadoff single to Perdomo before yanking an 0-1 four-seamer right into Corbin Carroll’s nitro zone, the three-time All-Star obliterating it to right for a two-run bomb to reduce the Yankees’ lead, 5-2. Rice made sure to immediately tilt the momentum back in his team’s favor. After falling behind 0-2, he stayed back on an elevated heater from E-Rod riding it out the other way and over the fence in left-center for a leadoff bomb, his 39th of the year, to give Cole some more of his cushion back, 6-2.
Cole settled down to work a scoreless third and fourth, helped in part by a sharp uptick in slider usage at the expense of some four-seamers as well as an impressive sliding catch in left-center by Spencer Jones in the third. He finally began dialing the fastball command to the corners in the fifth, striking out Tim Tawa and Lars Nootbaar on four-seamers to end the frame after Jesús Sánchez singled with one out. This allowed Lombard to restore the Yankees’ five run lead in the sixth, the rookie punishing a hanging curveball from E-Rod by lining the solo shot down the line it left and into the bullpen for his fourth of the year and third RBI on the night.
The four-seamer was the prime culprit for Cole in his previous two starts with a 68.2-percent hard-hit rate and just six whiffs, and that remained the case tonight. However, I believe it is Cole’s rustiness with his secondaries that is leading his four-seamer to get barreled. The fastball still has plenty of velocity — at 97 mph it’s a full tick above last season. I will grant that he has missed location in the zone on numerous occasions which hasn’t done him any favors.
However, after his last start, Cole identified a lack of chase and whiff against his secondaries as the reason his fastball is getting crushed. Hitters being able to lay off those chase pitches forces Cole to overuse the fastball in counts that favor the softer stuff, which in essence gives them the opportunity to hunt the heater when they should be defending against the breaker. When you can hunt a fastball in any count, chances are you are going to do damage when Cole misses his spot in the zone, the high velocity not much of a weapon when hitters’ bats are preemptively sped up.
Indeed, once he started commanding his slider and knuckle curve to the shadow of the zone in the middle innings, the hard contact against the fastball dried up. Having pitched a strong fifth and sixth and with his pitch count at 90, Boone saw no reason to overextend Cole and ended his night after six with his best innings freshest in mind. He finished night having pitched six innings, allowing two runs on four hits with no walks and six strikeouts.
Despite possessing one of the stingiest bullpens in baseball, the Diamondbacks decided that a five-run deficit in the seventh was too steep to justify using their high leverage arms. So, Zac Gallen made his first career relief appearance, the former All-Star in the midst of am injury-plagued, below-replacement-level campaign. He allowed a leadoff single to Goldschmidt and walked Ramos and Rice — again, both in full counts — to load the bases with one out. Aaron Boone sent out Ryan McMahon to pinch-hit for Rosario, and he hit a sharp grounder to first that Pavin Smith gloved but airmailed the underhand toss to Gallen covering first as all the runners were safe and a run scored on the error. Spencer Jones then appeared to ground into the inning-ending double play, but his hustle out of the box and down the line just beat the throw to pick up an RBI and make it 9-2.
Ryan Yarbrough pitched 1.1 innings in relief of Cole and worked himself into and out of trouble in the seventh. Arizona put runners on second and third as Nolan Arenado singled and Carroll doubled with one out. However, Yarbrough struck out Jose Fernandez and Tawa to strand the pair in scoring position. Rice smoked his fourth triple of the year in the ninth but was stranded at third by a McMahon strikeout. Michael Fulmer and Luis Gil recorded the final five outs of the game without allowing a baserunner to seal the win, 9-2. With the Rays having lost to the Red Sox earlier in the evening, the Yankees’ deficit is back to four games in the division, making that looming four-game set against Tampa in the Bronx even more high stakes.
Cam Schlittler looks to cement his AL Cy Young case tomorrow after Dylan Cease suffered his shortest start of the season on Friday. The Yankees ace will face off against Brandon Pfaadt with a slightly more reasonable game start time. First pitch is scheduled for 8:10 pm ET with the broadcast remaining on YES.
Yankees rout the D-Backs, 9-2, who's your Player of the Game?
Gerrit Cole pitched 6 innings of 2-run ball. George Lombard Jr. hit a two-run single and a solo homer. Ben Rice raked with a solo homer, triple, and two walks.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- Gerrit Cole had never surrendered seven home runs over a two-start span before his most recent outings, and with the playoffs around the corner, there was concern that the Yankees’ right-hander might have hit a wall.
Most of that came from outside the clubhouse. Yankees manager Aaron Boone affirmed Friday that Cole should expect to draw a start if his team lands in the American League Wild Card Series, and the veteran made good on his promise to fix the long-ball issue, pitching well in a 9-2 victory over the Diamondbacks at Chase Field on Friday night.
Hours after Cody Bellinger said the Yankees would have to “lean on each other” to overcome Aaron Judge’s absence, with the three-time AL MVP potentially set to miss the rest of the regular season with a right calf strain, the Bombers supported Cole with a five-run first inning.
Each of the first five batters reached base and scored against Eduardo Rodriguez. Ben Rice worked a bases-loaded walk, Amed Rosario lifted a run-scoring single and George Lombard Jr. stroked a two-run single -- part of a three-RBI night for the rookie, who launched a sixth-inning homer that chased Rodriguez.
Rice also slugged his team-leading 39th home run to support Cole, who had served up leadoff homers in his previous two starts. Having spent time focusing on his delivery and potential pitch-tipping issues since his last outing against the Mets, Cole set Arizona down in order during a 12-pitch first inning.
Corbin Carroll cracked a two-run homer in the second inning off Cole, but that was all the D-backs managed. Throwing 90 pitches (62 for strikes), Cole scattered four hits, walking none and striking out six.

item.content:encoded:
On Friday night, the New York Yankees are playing the first game of their series with the Arizona Diamondbacks at Chase Field.
They are coming off a series where they won two out of three games over the Minnesota Twins at Target Field.
New York Yankees Announced Chisholm Jr. Update
The Yankees continue to play without one of their best players, as Jazz Chisholm Jr. has been out since September 8 with an injury.
Ahead of Friday’s game, manager Aaron Boone shared the latest on the two-time MLB All-Star.
Bryan Hoch of MLB.com wrote: “Jazz Chisholm Jr. is “doing well” and should be activated on this homestand, Aaron Boone said.”
Before getting hurt, Chisholm Jr. had been batting .232 with 107 hits, 19 home runs, 55 RBIs, 68 runs and 40 stolen bases in 134 games.
MLB.com also wrote (on September 18): “Went on the IL on Sept. 10 and will have no baseball activities for 7-10 days. “Doing well,” Aaron Boone said Sept. 18, Chisholm’s fourth consecutive day of hitting. He has also been throwing.”
Looking At Chisholm Jr.
Chisholm Jr. is in the middle of his third season playing for the Yankees.
Prior to New York, he had spent the first 4.5 seasons of his career on the Miami Marlins.
In 2024, Chisholm Jr. helped the Yankees reach the World Series.
This winter, Chisholm Jr. will be among the most intriguing free agents to hit the market.
He will turn 29 in February.
Yankees On Friday
The Yankees are the second-place team in the American League East.
They have gone 88-64 in 152 games.
Following three games in Arizona, the Yankees will host the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday.

item.content:encoded:
New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone does not sound confident about Aaron Judge’s odds of returning this season.
Judge left in the middle of the Yankees’ Wednesday tilt against the Minnesota Twins with an injury the team initially labeled as right leg soreness. Two days later, the Yankees announced that they were placing Judge on the 10-day injured list.
With less than two weeks until the playoffs begin, reporters asked Boone Friday whether Judge would be back in the lineup in time for the postseason. The Yankees skipper did not sound convinced.
“I don’t know,” Boone responded, via USA Today’s Bob Nightengale. “I don’t have a timeline on it. I can’t predict anything. … I mean, we have no idea, we’re in the early stages. We’ll just obviously treat it and see what transpires.”
Boone spoke further about the Yankees learning to play without Judge, who has spent more than half the season on the mend.
“The reality is that we’ve had to play a lot of the season this year without him,’’ Boone said. “There’s no replacing a player as great as Aaron Judge, but you know we have high expectations that don’t change now. We have a lot of confidence in the people we run out there every day. We’re going to match up day in and day out, and the goal doesn’t change.”
The Yankees lost Judge for 84 games this season after he sustained a rib injury in April. He tried to play through the issue and had an unproductive May until the team decided to shut him down.
New York maintained a winning pace during that span, going 45-39 in the 84 games without its captain. But winning gets a lot harder once the lights get brighter in the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- Cam Schlittler sported a significant bruise on his right hamstring as he moved through the visiting clubhouse at Chase Field on Friday afternoon. It was a souvenir from his most recent start, which ended after the Mets’ Bo Bichette connected on a 111.5 mph comebacker.
That ball dented flesh, but Schlittler’s season has been so charmed, even the hard-hit balls are turning into outs. Bichette’s knock ricocheted to catcher Austin Wells, who tossed on to first base, sealing Schlittler’s six scoreless innings that day.
“It’s fun to watch. It’s fun to play behind,” Cody Bellinger said. “Even in the middle of the game, I was like, ‘This is unbelievable.’ You don’t really get that much.”
And while the league has had ample opportunity to take in Schlittler’s dominance, what impresses most from a distance of 60 feet and six inches?
“Probably the composure on the mound,” Wells said. “I think that’s the most impressive, besides obviously the numbers across the board. It’s just the way he handles every inning, every pitch. He expects the best every time he throws the ball. So it’s super impressive.”
That’s good news for the Yankees, who appear to be lining up Schlittler to start a potential Game 1 of the American League Wild Card Series against the Red Sox.
“You’ve got an ace at the top that’s pitched like that, that’s a good place to start,” manager Aaron Boone said. “He’s been dominant. I think he’s just continued to get better, year in and year out.”
“The expectation is to make the playoffs, and the expectation is to win a championship,” Schlittler said. “We’re in a good spot if we keep playing the way we’re playing.”
With Schlittler deep into his longest season yet, Wells believes his batterymate is finding new layers of sharpness.
“I think we’ve seen games where he doesn’t have the best command, but he still gets through it,” Wells said. “There’s another layer to that command piece, that makes it effectively a little bit wild sometimes. I think when he continues to improve that, he’s just going to continue to get better.”
Schlittler’s 1.95 ERA is the second-lowest by a Yankee through 31 starts since Ron Guidry’s 1.71 ERA in 1978, when “Louisiana Lightning” won the Cy Young and finished second in the MVP race to Jim Rice of the Red Sox.
It was the 21st time Schlittler has allowed one run or fewer. That’s a franchise record, and over the last 110 years, only three pitchers age 25 or younger have had as many: Blake Snell (2018), Dean Chance (1964) and Babe Ruth (1916).
Yet Boone said he’s not surprised by Schlittler’s performance, saying it has been largely in line with what the Yankees saw after his late-season callup in 2025.
“He had about as dominant a postseason outing as you could against the Red Sox, and he has carried that right into this year,” Boone said. “He’s got great stuff, he’s a tremendous competitor and he has a real good way about him -- an ability to make adjustments start to start, not be overwhelmed by a result start to start, and he’s put it all together for a full season now at this level.”

item.content:encoded:
Los Yankees de Nueva York volverán a jugar sin su capitán en un momento clave de la temporada. Aaron Judge será colocado nuevamente en la lista de lesionados de 10 días, esta vez debido a una distensión en la pantorrilla derecha, informó el equipo este viernes. La decisión llega apenas unos días después de que el tres veces MVP de la Liga Americana regresara de una lesión que lo mantuvo fuera durante gran parte de la campaña.
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Dodgers ya son campeones de la División Oeste!
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¿Cómo cambia el último comodín de la Nacional en Padres vs. Marlins?
Suscríbete al Newsletter de Unanimo y recibe gratis las últimas noticias. Dale click aquí
Judge había vuelto al terreno el 8 de septiembre, después de pasar alrededor de 100 días fuera por una fractura por estrés en la primera costilla derecha. El jardinero había evitado una asignación de rehabilitación en las Ligas Menores y regresó directamente al lineup de Nueva York para enfrentar a los Rockies de Colorado.
Sin embargo, su regreso duró poco. El miércoles 16 de septiembre, durante el encuentro contra los Twins de Minnesota, Judge fue retirado en la sexta entrada y sustituido por un bateador emergente. Después del partido explicó que había sentido rigidez en la parte baja de la pierna derecha desde la primera entrada y que, después de hablarlo con el equipo, consideró que lo mejor era abandonar el encuentro para evitar que la molestia se agravara.
La nueva lesión representa otro golpe para un jugador que apenas estaba retomando ritmo competitivo. Desde su regreso, Judge disputó seis encuentros y registró 4 imparables en 23 turnos (.174), un cuadrangular y varios ponches. En el balance de la temporada, suma .241 de promedio, .360 de porcentaje de embasado, .511 de slugging, 18 jonrones y 41 carreras impulsadas en 66 partidos.
El momento de la lesión también es particularmente relevante para los Yankees. Nueva York llegó a la jornada del viernes cinco juegos por detrás de los Rays de Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, por lo que la ausencia de Judge se producirá durante una parte importante de la pelea por la posición en la tabla. El equipo, además, tendrá que afrontar una serie de cuatro encuentros contra Tampa Bay la próxima semana.
Ver esta publicación en Instagram
La buena noticia, al menos sobre el papel, es que la colocación en la lista de lesionados puede hacerse de manera retroactiva al jueves 17 de septiembre. Esto significa que la fecha más temprana para que Judge vuelva sería el 27 de septiembre, precisamente el último partido de la temporada regular, cuando los Yankees enfrenten a los Orioles de Baltimore.
El problema es que todavía no existe certeza sobre su regreso. Aaron Boone no ha establecido un calendario concreto para la recuperación de su capitán y tampoco aseguró que Judge pueda estar disponible para la postemporada. El Wild Card de la Liga Americana está programado para comenzar el 29 de septiembre, apenas dos días después del último encuentro de temporada regular.
Judge había sido una pieza fundamental para Nueva York antes de su primera lesión. La fractura de la costilla derecha lo llevó a la lista de lesionados en junio, después de que el jugador intentara competir durante varias semanas con molestias. Finalmente, los estudios determinaron que se trataba de una fractura por estrés, lo que provocó que se perdiera más de tres meses de actividad.
Ahora los Yankees tendrán que afrontar nuevamente el cierre de la temporada sin su principal figura ofensiva. El equipo deberá esperar la evolución de la pantorrilla derecha de Judge mientras continúa la lucha por definir su posición rumbo a octubre. Por ahora, el 27 de septiembre aparece como su posible fecha más temprana de regreso, pero su participación en la postemporada permanece en duda.

item.content:encoded:
Yankees superstar Aaron Judge will be placed on the 10-day injured list on Saturday, the Yankees announced Friday evening prior to their game in Arizona. This comes two days after Judge exited in the middle of a game due to a right calf strain. Judge missed more than three months earlier this season with a wrist issue and played just seven games before landing back on the injured list.
There are only 10 days left in the season, but the Yankees can backdate the transaction, which would make the three-time MVP eligible to return from the injured list on the final day of the regular season, Sept. 27, though his body would need to cooperate. The Wild Card Series, which the Yankees will play in unless they can track down the Rays in the AL East, will begin on Tuesday, Sept. 29.
We can't be sure that the level of severity is similar, but for what it's worth, Judge had a strained calf in 2020 and missed roughly three weeks. A similar timeline this year, would see Judge return in the middle of the ALDS (if the Yankees reach the round).
As for when the Yankees expect him back? They don't know.
"I don't know," manager Aaron Boone told reporters on Friday. "I'm not going to predict anything."
Judge this season has 66 games played, hitting .241/.360/.511 (140 OPS+) with 18 homers, 41 RBI and 1.9 WAR. Judge homered against the Twins on Monday, but he was hitting just .174/.208/.304 in 24 plate appearances since returning from the wrist injury.
He has dealt with injuries in the past, but this season marks his lowest games played in a non-COVID season since he was called up late in the season as a rookie.
The Yankees have already clinched a playoff berth. They have an outside shot at winning the AL East and the top seed in the AL. They trail the Rays by five games, but there's a four-game series in Yankee Stadium next week. Judge will be sidelined for the entire series.
Of course, the Yankees without Judge are a different team. They are 41-25 when he starts and 47-39 when he doesn't. He's one of the most important players to a team in all of baseball.
The Yankees have a three-game stop in Arizona before finishing at home with a four-game series against the Rays and a three-game series against the Orioles.

item.content:encoded:
Sep 18, 2026, 9:06 PM ET
According to Bryan Hoch, New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone confirmed on Friday that second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (thumb) is expected to return during their upcoming homestand. It sounds like Chisholm is doing well in his recovery from a right thumb strain that has sidelined him since early September. Boone didn't give an exact timetable, but more information should be known following the weekend series in Arizona. It sounds like fantasy managers still in the playoff picture might be able to get something out of Chisholm before the end of the season. There should be more information on his status as he continues to ramp up his activities.--Andy Webb
Source: Bryan Hoch
More Recent News
Sep 18, 2026, 9:33 PM ET
Pittsburgh Pirates starting pitcher Braxton Ashcraft (arm) is unlikely to return to the mound this season, Kevin Gorman of TribLive.com reports. Ashcraft appears to be making progress as he was able to play catch from 90 feet on Friday. Despite that, Ashcraft is unlikely to make enough progress to get back on the mound before the end of the regular season. Ashcraft has been out since early September due to right arm discomfort. Ashcraft is probably done for the year, but he did post a breakout campaign for the Pirates this season. Across 28 starts, Ashcraft posted a 3.65 ERA, 1.09 WHIP, and a 173/35 K/BB ratio across 165.1 innings of work.--Andy Webb
Source: Kevin Gorman
Pete Fairbanks to Undergo Surgery


Andy Webb




Sep 18, 2026, 9:24 PM ET
Miami Marlins relief pitcher Pete Fairbanks (hand) will undergo surgery to treat thoracic outlet syndrome, Christina De Nicola of MLB.com reports. Fairbanks landed on the Injured List on Tuesday with nerve irritation in his right hand. Now, the right-hander will undergo surgery to treat the injury. Fairbanks is done for the season, and he could miss part of the 2027 season as well while he recovers from surgery. Fairbanks posted a 6.31 ERA, 1.35 WHIP, and a 57/22 K/BB ratio with 19 saves in 46 appearances with the Marlins this season. Calvin Faucher and Michael Petersen are the favorites to see save chances down the stretch in Miami.--Andy Webb
Source: Christina De Nicola
Sep 18, 2026, 9:13 PM ET
New York Yankees manager Aaron Boone said on Friday that pitcher Ryan Weathers (forearm) is unlikely to pitch again before the end of the regular season, Bryan Hoch of MLB.com reports. Weathers is currently working his way back from a forearm flexor strain that has sidelined him since late August. The Yankees were hopeful that Weathers could return in a bullpen role, but that doesn't seem to be in the cards anymore. There is still a chance that Weathers returns in time to help the Yankees during the postseason. He probably won't have enough time to build up to become a starter, but something is better than nothing. Fantasy managers in redraft formats who are still holding Weathers can safely move on.--Andy Webb
Source: Bryan Hoch
Aroldis Chapman "Not Worried At All" About Lat Strain


Keith Hernandez




Sep 18, 2026, 7:39 PM ET
Boston Red Sox left-handed closer Aroldis Chapman (lat) said he is "not worried at all" about his lat strain that made him unavailable to pitch in Thursday's late-inning comeback win over the Texas Rangers, according to Sean McAdam of MassLive.com. Chapman said he has felt improvement since it first popped up on Tuesday, and he is confident he will pitch again before the end of the 2026 regular season. While the 38-year-old veteran southpaw appears to have dodged a bullet, it is unclear how quickly he might be available to pick up another save for fantasy managers playing for a championship late in the season. If Chapman misses more time, right-hander Garrett Whitlock, who picked up his fourth save of the year in Texas on Thursday, is expected to get the first crack at more save opportunities. Chapman continues to defy Father Time in 2026 and has been great with a 1.95 ERA, 1.14 WHIP, 34 saves, and 68 strikeouts in his 50 2/3 innings out of the bullpen in his second year in Boston. Last year, Chapman had a 1.17 ERA and 32 saves.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MassLive.com - Sean McAdam
Joshua Baez Lands on Injured List With Oblique Strain


Keith Hernandez




Sep 18, 2026, 7:27 PM ET
The St. Louis Cardinals announced on Friday that they placed rookie outfielder Joshua Baez (oblique) on the 10-day injured list with a left-oblique strain and recalled infielder Cesar Prieto from Triple-A Memphis in a corresponding move. Baez will most likely miss the rest of the 2026 season for the Cardinals after injuring his oblique during Wednesday's contest against the San Francisco Giants. The 23-year-old, who is ranked as the team's No. 3 prospect at MLB Pipeline, hit three home runs against the division-rival Chicago Cubs in his major-league debut on Aug. 15 and ended up hitting .230 (23-for-100) with seven home runs, seven doubles, 18 RBI, two stolen bases, 18 runs scored, four walks, and 33 strikeouts in his first 29 games MLB games across 108 plate appearances. The 6-foot-3, 220-pounder will have breakout potential in 2027 for his pure power upside, but fantasy managers might also have to be pretty patient with his high strikeout rate.--Keith Hernandez
Source: St. Louis Cardinals
Hunter Goodman Returns From his Thumb Injury on Friday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 18, 2026, 7:17 PM ET
Colorado Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman (thumb) is doing the catching for right-hander Gabriel Hughes and is hitting cleanup for the team in Friday's series opener at Coors Field against the Seattle Mariners and right-hander Bryan Woo, according to MLB.com. Goodman is back in action to begin the weekend after missing four of the previous five games with a right-thumb injury that has been bothering him recently. It has affected the power-hitting catcher at the plate, as he has gone 6-for-42 (.143) with two home runs, two doubles, a triple, eight RBI, six runs scored, three walks, and 12 strikeouts in 11 games in September. Still, the 26-year-old former fourth-rounder from Memphis should be returned to all starting fantasy lineups as the best power-hitting catcher in the game. Goodman is returning to a .245/.312/.529 slash line, an .841 OPS, 38 home runs, 81 RBI, 80 runs scored, and even five stolen bases in 482 at-bats in 2026. He has never faced Woo in his career.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Colson Montgomery Back in the Lineup Against Tigers


Keith Hernandez




Sep 18, 2026, 7:12 PM ET
Chicago White Sox infielder Colson Montgomery (wrist) is starting at shortstop and batting eighth in Friday's contest against the division-rival Detroit Tigers and left-hander Andrew Sears, per MLB.com. It is good news to see Montgomery back in Chicago's starting lineup after he was pulled from Wednesday's game against the division-rival Cleveland Guardians following being hit by a pitch on his left wrist. Thankfully, the 24-year-old avoided any fractures in his wrist and has returned following a scheduled day off on Thursday. Fantasy managers will want to get Montgomery back in their lineups this weekend for the stretch run, despite the fact that he has not hit a home run in his last 10 games. The former 22nd overall pick in 2021 is hitting only .203 (109-for-536) in his first full big-league season in 2026, but he has done damage with 31 home runs and 84 RBI across his 144 games played and 604 plate appearances for the ChiSox. However, he hit an even .200 (20-for-100) in 26 games in August and has gone just 5-for-49 (.102) with two homers, seven RBI, six walks, and 26 strikeouts in 15 games so far in September.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Jac Caglianone Out With Hand Injury


Keith Hernandez




Sep 18, 2026, 6:04 PM ET
Kansas City Royals first baseman/outfielder Jac Caglianone (hand) is out of Friday's starting lineup against the Pittsburgh Pirates due to a hand injury that he suffered on Thursday night, manager Matt Quatraro told Royals broadcaster Joel Goldberg. "It was in the dugout after one of the at-bats. It was my decision to not play him today," Quatraro said. Nick Loftin is making the start in right field for the Royals and will bat eighth in the order against Pirates right-hander Paul Skenes. For now, fantasy managers should consider Caglianone to be day-to-day and check back to see if he is available to play as the series continues in the Steel City on Saturday. The 23-year-old former sixth overall pick from Florida has had a great first full season in the big leagues in 2026, hitting .277/.328/.483 with an .811 OPS, 23 home runs, 70 RBI, 66 runs scored, and six stolen bases across 484 at-bats. However, he has been banged up lately and is limping to the finish line. Cags has gone 4-for-27 (.148) with four RBI, a walk, and 11 strikeouts in 10 games so far in September.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Joel Goldberg
Aaron Judge Going on the Injured List With Calf Strain


Keith Hernandez




Sep 18, 2026, 5:39 PM ET
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge (calf) is going on the 10-day injured list on Saturday with a strained right calf, according to Chris Kirschner of The Athletic. It will be the second time that Judge has gone on the IL this year, with the first time coming from a stress fracture in his rib that cost him most of the season. The three-time MVP injured his calf during Wednesday's contest against the Minnesota Twins. The right-handed slugger will now rest up until the playoffs begin in October, but there is no guarantee that he will be ready to roll by then either. In Judge's absence for the rest of September, Heliot Ramos should see most of the playing time in right field in the Bronx. Former top prospect Jasson Dominguez should also be called up from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre to give the Yanks more outfield depth. Judge will finish his 11th year in the majors with a .241/.360/.511 slash line, an 871 OPS, 18 home runs, 41 RBI, 45 runs scored, and five stolen bases in just 66 games played and 285 plate appearances.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Chris Kirschner
Dansby Swanson Activated And Starting on Friday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 18, 2026, 5:02 PM ET
Chicago Cubs shortstop Dansby Swanson (oblique) has been activated from the 10-day injured list, with third baseman BJ Murray Jr. being optioned to Triple-A Iowa in a corresponding move, according to Meghan Montemurro of The Chicago Tribune. Swanson is starting at shortstop and batting ninth in Friday's series opener on the road against the division-rival Cincinnati Reds and right-hander Chase Burns, per MLB.com. He will make his first start since being sidelined in mid-August with a Grade 2 left-oblique strain. Swanson will return as Chicago's primary shortstop, pushing Nico Hoerner back to second-base duties. Without going on a rehab assignment, fantasy managers should not be surprised if Swanson struggles at the plate upon his return. The 32-year-old veteran is returning to a .216/.300/.404 slash line with a .704 OPS, 18 home runs, 66 RBI, 78 runs scored, and 17 stolen bases in his 403 at-bats this season. Hitting in the nine-hole against Burns will definitely not endear him to any DFS managers on Friday.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Chicago Tribune - Meghan Montemurro
Cade Cavalli Agrees to Four-Year Extension With Nationals


Keith Hernandez




Sep 18, 2026, 4:50 PM ET
The Washington Nationals announced on Friday that they agreed to a four-year contract extension with right-hander Cade Cavalli through the 2030 season that includes a club option for the 2031 season. The deal is worth $47 million guaranteed and $70 million if the options are picked up, according to Spencer Nusbaum of The Athletic. The 28-year-old secures his future in D.C. after a breakout 2026 campaign. The former 22nd overall pick from the University of Oklahoma in 2020 has gone 12-5 this year with a 3.12 ERA (3.33 FIP), 1.17 WHIP, and 194:48 K:BB in 164 2/3 innings pitched across his 31 starts in his first full season in the big leagues. Cavalli only made one start in his debut season in 2022 with the Nats, did not pitch at all in 2023 due to Tommy John surgery, and made only 10 starts in Washington last year. He has posted a career-high 28.2% strikeout rate and maintained the command that he showed in a small sample size in 2025 by walking 7.0% of the batters he has faced. With a longer leash in 2027, Cavalli could be even better if he stays healthy.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Washington Nationals
Willson Contreras Held Out of Friday's Lineup


Keith Hernandez




Sep 18, 2026, 3:39 PM ET
Boston Red Sox first baseman Willson Contreras (hand) is not in the team's starting lineup for Friday's series opener against the division-rival Tampa Bay Rays, according to MLB.com. Nick Sogard will man first base for the BoSox and bat second against Rays left-hander Ian Seymour. It should not be a huge surprise that Contreras is not starting on Friday after he was pulled from Thursday's win over the Texas Rangers after being hit on the right hand by a pitch late in the game. Thankfully, X-rays came back negative, and Contreras was diagnosed with a bruised hand. Fantasy managers should consider him day-to-day and check back on him to see if he is playing in Game 2 of the series in Tampa on Saturday. The 34-year-old veteran and former catcher has battled through some injuries this year but has still been one of Boston's best bats in 2026, as he is currently hitting .276/.387/.518 with a .905 OPS, 27 home runs, 81 RBI, 68 runs scored, and three steals in his 446 at-bats in his first year in Beantown. However, he did hit just .217 (18-for-83) with three homers, 12 RBI, 11 walks, and 26 strikeouts in 23 games in August, and he has played in only four games so far in September.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Chase DeLauter Returns From Wrist Injury on Friday


Keith Hernandez




Sep 18, 2026, 3:24 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians rookie outfielder Chase DeLauter (wrist) is starting in right field and batting third for the Guardians on Friday against the visiting Athletics and right-hander Mason Barnett, per MLB.com. DeLauter has missed some time in recent weeks with a sprained right wrist, but he is back in action to begin the weekend series against the A's after missing each of the last two games on Tuesday and Wednesday against the division-rival Chicago White Sox. The 24-year-old former first-rounder has been money for Cleveland in his first year in the big leagues in 2026, slashing .289/.362/.453 with an .815 OPS, 14 home runs, 62 RBI, 57 runs scored, and 11 stolen bases across his 464 at-bats. DeLauter has only gone deep three times in 45 second-half games, but he has hit lefties well and is coming off a month of August in which he slashed .363/.440/.538 with a .977 OPS, two homers, and nine RBI in 22 games played. If his wrist injury does not impact him the rest of the way, DeLauter will be looking to put a bow on a strong first year in the bigs.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com
Sep 18, 2026, 1:35 PM ET
Washington Nationals infield prospect Seaver King hit his 20th homer of the season on Wednesday night at Triple-A Rochester to put an exclamation point on his breakout 2026 season in the minor leagues. Between Double-A Harrisburg and Rochester this season, King has hit .306 with those 20 homers and 73 RBI to go with 85 runs scored and 15 stolen bases. It's a complete stat line from the Wake Forest grad, but he hasn't received a call-up yet from the Nationals. He is the No. 4 prospect in the Nationals system and has a 50-grade hit tool with 45-grade power and 70-grade speed. Look for King's strong minor league season at age 23 to give him a shot at breaking camp with the major league team in 2027. He has done everything he can to prove worthy of the opportunity and would be a good fantasy player to target in 2027 drafts.--Brian Buckey - RotoBaller
Source: Minor League Baseball
Sep 18, 2026, 1:28 PM ET
New York Yankees shortstop prospect Dax Kilby missed much of the 2026 season with a hamstring injury but returned to hit four homers and 26 RBI in 124 at-bats with a .242 batting average and 27 runs scored with 12 stolen bases. The 19-year-old was the first-round pick of the Yankees in the 2025 MLB Draft and slots in at No. 2 on the team's prospect list. He has a 60-grade hit tool with 60-grade speed and 50-grade power. Speed looks to be a big part of the youngster's game, and swiping 12 bags in his limited time this season proves that. He looks to be a few years away, at least from a big-league debut, but he looks like a potential five-category star at the shortstop position. Kilby looks like a strong dynasty league addition with the potential to be a fantasy stud.--Brian Buckey - RotoBaller
Source: Minor League Baseball
JoJo Parker Hitting Nicely at High-A Vancouver

Sep 18, 2026, 1:20 PM ET
Toronto Blue Jays shortstop prospect JoJo Parker has shown off his hitting skills at High-A Vancouver since his recent call-up at age 20. In 21 games at Vancouver, Parker is hitting .316, which is a big improvement from his .256 batting average at Single-A Dunedin for most of the year. Parker has combined across both levels to steal 28 bases this season and score 85 runs. The left-handed hitter is the top overall prospect for the Blue Jays and has a 55-grade hit tool and 55-grade power. At 6-foot-2 and 200 pounds, Parker has nice size at the shortstop position and has done enough with his bat and on the basepaths to prove why he is so highly regarded as a prospect. Look for Parker to debut with the Blue Jays in a few years, and he should be added to the list of future star fantasy shortstops.--Brian Buckey - RotoBaller
Source: Minor League Baseball
Sep 18, 2026, 1:11 PM ET
Cincinnati Reds catcher prospect Alfredo Duno came back from a right hamstring injury on August 26 and since then has been red-hot with the bat for Double-A Chattanooga. Since that return date, Duno has hit 20-for-55 (.364) with no homers and six RBI. Altogether this season, between two levels of the minors, the 20-year-old is hitting .281 with 19 homers and 61 RBI in 363 at bats with 64 runs scored. The right-handed hitter is the top overall prospect in the Reds system and figures to be their catcher of the future. He has a 55-grade hit tool with 55-grade power. The Venezuelan is the No. 3 prospect in the Dodgers' organization and boasts 60-grade speed with a 55-grade hit tool and 55-grade power. Sep 18, 2026, 12:51 PM ET
Atlanta Braves outfield prospect Eric Hartman has had a good minor league season at age 20, but has struggled since his call-up in early August to Double-A Columbus. In 34 games with Columbus, the left-handed hitter has two homers and 10 RBI while hitting just .182. He does, however, have 18 stolen bases, which is a great sign despite the struggles in the batting average department. Hartman is the top prospect in the Braves' system and boasts 70-grade speed with a 55-grade hit tool and 50-grade power. Between Columbus and High-A Rome this season, Hartman has shown off that speed with 56 combined stolen bases to go with 26 homers and 74 RBI and a combined .249 batting average. Hartman looks like the real deal with his stolen base threat and that makes him a potential five-tool player and fantasy contributor a few years down the road.--Brian Buckey - RotoBaller
Source: Minor League Baseball
Aroldis Chapman Unavailable Due to Lat Issue


Keith Hernandez




Sep 17, 2026, 11:44 PM ET
Boston Red Sox left-handed closer Aroldis Chapman (lat) was unavailable to pitch in Thursday night's game in Texas against the Rangers due to a lat issue, interim manager Chad Tracy told The Boston Globe's Tim Healey. Chapman had been dealing with it for a couple of days, and the Red Sox will be "conservative" with it, according to Tracy. With Chapman unavailable on Thursday night, right-hander Garrett Whitlock came in to pick up the save, throwing a clean inning with one walk to lower his season ERA to 1.78. The Red Sox will need Chapman down the stretch as they hunt for a playoff spot in the American League, but it sounds like the veteran closer might not be available going into Friday's series opener against the division-rival Tampa Bay Rays. The nine-time All-Star and two-time closer of the year has been excellent for the BoSox as their primary closer in 2026, posting a 1.95 ERA (2.60 FIP), a 1.14 WHIP, 34 saves, 68 strikeouts, and 23 walks in his 50 2/3 innings pitched in his 17th year in the big leagues. Fantasy managers desperate for some saves at this juncture should look to pick up Whitlock off the waiver wire.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey

item.content:encoded:
Yankees manager Aaron Boone delivered some injury updates ahead of Friday's series opener with the Diamondbacks in Arizona…
Jazz returning soon
Although the Yankees are losing Aaron Judge, likely, for the remainder of the regular season, they'll be activating Jazz Chisholm Jr. very soon.
Boone confirmed that the second baseman will return to the club during the team's final homestand, which starts Tuesday against the Tampa Bay Rays. The Yankees skipper said Chisholm is doing well and Friday was his fourth day in a row hitting. He's done a couple of days of throwing already and is "really close."
Chisholm was placed on the IL back on Sept. 10 with a sprained thumb after he jammed it sliding head-first into second base.
The Yankees infielder was on a tear before he was injured, slashing .375/.464/.500 with a home run over his last seven games. For the season, he's batting .232/.312/.403 with an OPS of .715 to go along with his 19 home runs, 40 stolen bases and 55 RBI.
The return of Chisholm would raise some questions regarding the team's roster. While Chisholm could take over for Max Schuemann, who is being called up to take Judge's spot, Anthony Volpe has been playing second base almost regularly in Chisholm's stead. How Boone juggles the playing time for both players will be worth monitoring.
Bad Weathers
On the other side of the return spectrum, LHP Ryan Weathers is "unlikely" to pitch before the end of the regular season, Boone revealed.
Weathers was placed on the IL in late August due to a left forearm flexor strain, and although the southpaw has made strides, there's not enough time on the regular season calendar to get him on the mound before the postseason starts. Boone did say that Weathers will have another side session on Saturday, and that could determine whether the team will use him in the playoffs.
"We'll see what our needs are and how he looks, and if we feel like he's ready to come in and be a contributor," Boone said.
In 25 starts this season, Weathers has pitched to a 3.60 ERA and a 1.22 WHIP. His last seven starts have been tremendous, though, pitching to a 2.27 ERA and a 1.18 WHIP.
Grisham rising
And finally, Trent Grisham is nearing a return as well.
Boone said the veteran outfielder is "pretty far" into his running progression and is doing well. He could be in play to be activated before the end of the season.
Grisham was placed on the IL on Sept. 5 with a right hamstring strain, the same injury he suffered back in June this season. If Grisham is able to return on the upcoming homestand, Boone will, again, have to juggle the roster as Spencer Jones and Heliot Ramos have played regularly in his absence. Though Judge's injury gives Grisham a runway to start, especially against right-handers.
In 121 games this season, Grisham is slashing .211/.308/.395 with an OPS of .703.

item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge is going on the 10-day injured list with a right calf strain, the Yankees announced Friday, just seven games after he returned from a three-month stay on the IL with a right rib stress fracture.
Access the Yankees beat like never before
Join Post Sports+ for exciting subscriber-only features, including real-time texting with Greg Joyce about the inside buzz on the Yankees.
With only nine games left in the regular season after Friday, Judge’s injury threatens to be a serious blow to the Yankees’ October hopes and dreams.
The earliest Judge can be activated off the IL — he will officially be placed on it Saturday, but retroactive to Thursday — is in time for Game 162, though there is doubt over whether he will even be ready in time for the start of the playoffs.
“I don’t know,” Aaron Boone said Friday at Chase Field.
Boone would not divulge a timeline for Judge, nor the grade of his strain. But after he received treatment on his calf during Thursday’s off day, it became clear there was not enough improvement, at which point they decided to send him for tests that revealed the strain.
The AL wild-card series, which the Yankees are all but assured to play in with their chances of catching the Rays for the division slim, begins on Sept. 29. Once again, Judge will be racing the clock to try to get back in time, creating major concerns for the Yankees as they head down the stretch without their best player.
“There’s no replacing a player as great as Aaron Judge, but we have high expectations that don’t change now,” Boone said. “We have a lot of confidence in the people we run out there every day and how we’re going to match up day in and day out, and the goal doesn’t change.”
When Judge spent most of the summer months on the IL, the Yankees’ offense largely cratered without him, though they had started to break out of their malaise shortly before he returned on Sept. 8.
Judge’s injury will create further scrutiny as to whether he should have gone on a rehab assignment instead of coming straight back into games. The captain was adamant about not wanting to waste time playing in minor league games, and the Yankees – who could not force Judge to go on a rehab assignment – tried to ease him back in carefully. They played him for six innings his first game back – much to his chagrin – then eight innings, then an off day. Judge then played four straight games through Monday’s playoff clincher before the Yankees sat him again on Tuesday, after which they were hopeful he would essentially be a full go.
But then came the nightmare, when Judge felt some calf tightness while playing the field in the bottom of the first inning and then by the top of the sixth, was pinch hit for by Heliot Ramos.
Before the injury, Judge was still trying to lock in his timing at the plate after a long layoff, batting 4-for-23 (.174) with a .513 OPS and one home run. These final three series were supposed to be about getting him in a good spot for the postseason, but now he will spend them getting treatment and rehabbing in hopes of playing again.
Fellow Yankees slugger Giancarlo Stanton suffered a calf strain in late April and has not played another game since, though he was initially on the verge of a return in June before suffering two more calf strains since.
Judge, after leaving Wednesday’s game against the Twins early, likened the issue to something he would deal with in spring training while building up his workload, except it is now September.
In the meantime, the Yankees started Ramos in right field on Friday against Diamondbacks lefty Eduardo Rodríguez, and he will likely get the majority of the time there down the stretch.
Even before Judge’s injury, the Yankees were already dealing with a few players trying to make a comeback in time for the playoffs, including Jazz Chisholm Jr. (right thumb sprain), Trent Grisham (right hamstring strain) and Ryan Weathers (left forearm flexor strain). Grisham, who could be ready by next week, now has a potential lane to come back in center field, bumping Spencer Jones to right. Chisholm is also expected to be activated when the Yankees return home.
Max Schuemann will join the Yankees on Saturday to take Judge’s roster spot.
“We’re gonna have to find a way,” Cody Bellinger said. “I think the talent in this locker room speaks for itself, and I’m fully confident that we have enough talent in here that we can go out and win and beat anybody.”

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are out West on Friday night to begin a weekend series with the Arizona Diamondbacks.
Ahead of the matchup, New York received some bad news as superstar Aaron Judge heads back to the IL with a calf strain. Yankees manager Aaron Boone also made a few notable changes to his starting lineup for the series opener.
Yankees Announce Paul Goldschmidt Decision
After spending pretty much the entire season in a platoon role and not starting the last time the Yankees played on Wednesday, veteran slugger Paul Goldschmidt is in the lineup Friday, starting at first base and batting leadoff.
He’ll bat in front of Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, and Ben Rice, who will move into the cleanup spot.
Here’s the full Yankees lineup:
Via Underdog MLB: “Yankees 9/18 P. Goldschmidt 1B C. Bellinger LF H. Ramos RF B. Rice DH A. Rosario 3B S. Jones CF G. Lombard Jr. SS A. Wells C A. Volpe 2B G. Cole SP.”
Yankees 9/18
P. Goldschmidt 1B
C. Bellinger LF
H. Ramos RF
B. Rice DH
A. Rosario 3B
S. Jones CF
G. Lombard Jr. SS
A. Wells C
A. Volpe 2B
G. Cole SP
— Underdog MLB (@UnderdogMLB) September 18, 2026
Goldschmidt’s 2026 Season
In his 16th MLB season and his second as a member of the Yankees, Goldschmidt has appeared in 101 games for New York, and across 332 at-bats, he’s hitting .253 with 42 runs, 84 hits, 18 home runs, and 50 RBIs while slugging .458 and maintaining a .773 OPS.
Looking at the Yankees
New York enters Friday’s contest with the D-backs holding an 88-64 overall record. They sit 5.0 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for the AL East division lead and the No. 1 overall seed in the American League.
Currently, the Yankees hold the top Wild Card spot, and if the season ended today, they’d host a best-of-three series at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx against, coincidentally enough, the Boston Red Sox in what would mark a rematch of the 2025 postseason.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees could make a surprising move on Anthony Volpe.
Volpe has had success since being recalled, but George Lombard Jr. has taken over as the starting shortstop. So, Volpe's future in New York is very much up in the air.
New York will begin a three-game road series against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday.
New York Yankees Surprise Anthony Volpe Decision
Although Volpe has been playing better, he isn't guaranteed a spot on the Yankees playoff roster.
After New York clinched a playoff spot, Yankees analysts Bryan Hoch and Patrick Donnelly of MLB.com revealed the likely playoff roster, and they didn't have Volpe on it.
What could the postseason roster look like?
C: Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez
1B: Luis García Jr., Paul Goldschmidt
2B: Jazz Chisholm Jr.
3B: Ryan McMahon, Amed Rosario
SS: George Lombard Jr., José Caballero
OF: Cody Bellinger, Spencer Jones, Aaron Judge, Heliot Ramos
DH: Ben Rice
SP: Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole
RP: David Bednar, Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn, Tim Hill, Ryan Yarbrough, Clarke Schmidt, Michael Fulmer, Ryan Weathers, Will Warren
The Yankees leaving Volpe off the playoff roster would be a disappointing outcome for the shortstop. It also could signal the end of his tenure in New York as Lombard is the shortstop of the future.
Volpe is hitting .253 with 2 home runs and 26 RBIs this season with the Yankees.
New York Right Now
The Yankees have clinched a playoff spot as New York will be hosting a Wild Card series again.
"Every year you go through a lot, it seems like. But we've been through a lot this year with injuries, with adversity," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "But credit to them for coming together. Through all the ups and downs, they've been a together group. I feel like they've developed a lot of grit over the season."
However, despite clinching a playoff spot, the Yankees made it clear the job isn't finished. New York likely won't win the AL East again, which is frustrating, but the Yankees have confidence they can go on a deep playoff run.
The Yankees are 88-64 and 5 games back of the Tampa Bay Rays for the top spot in the AL East.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — Aaron Judge is going back on the shelf.
The Yankees’ captain will be placed on the 10-day injured list with a right calf strain on Saturday, the team announced Friday. While an official move hasn’t been made yet, multiple sources told the Daily News that utilityman Max Schuemann will be recalled from Triple-A to take Judge’s place.
Judge, now ineligible to return until the final game of the regular season, suffered what the Yankees initially called a right lower leg injury during the team’s extra-inning loss to the Twins on Wednesday. The slugger said he first felt something while playing the field in the first inning, but he didn’t exit the game until Heliot Ramos pinch-hit for him in the sixth inning.
Judge could be seen grimacing on a check swing during the third inning and hobbling in the outfield during the fifth inning. Aaron Boone said he wasn’t made of Judge’s injury until just before the right fielder was pulled from the game; the skipper noticed the hobbling during the fifth frame.
“I tried to kind of play it off and see how long we could go, because these games are important down the stretch,” Judge said Wednesday. “But in talking it over, I thought it’d be the right move to come out so we don’t cost the team in the field or on the basepaths.
“I didn’t think it was smart to push it too much here.”
Judge’s return to the IL comes with him just seven games removed from a 99-day absence for a stress fracture in his first right rib. That injury sidelined him from May 31 through Sept. 7.
On Wednesday, Judge, 4-for-23 (.174) with one home run and three RBI since coming back, compared his new injury to the types of nagging issues that pop up during spring training and at the start of the season when players start ramping up their bodies. He has been doing just that since returning from his rib injury on Sept. 8.
“We’re still trying to ramp up, so there’s going to be little things like this that come up,” said Judge, who got his wish and skipped a rehab assignment for his rib.
Judge also only faced live pitching once before returning from his rib injury. He did not play in full games his first two days back, and he had off on Sept. 10 and Sept. 15.
Asked on Wednesday if his new injury made him rethink his rehab process, Judge told The News, “People blow out their calves and blow out their quads in rehab assignments, so I don’t think taking a game in Double-A will change any of that.”
He added that he felt his build-up has been gradual, as he had felt asymptomatic for weeks before returning.
“That’s what we kind of did with playing the [seven] innings, playing the eight innings,” Judge said, referring to his planned early exits in his first two games back, the first of which he said he was “not happy” about the night of.
The Yankees had one of the worst offenses in baseball during Judge’s last IL stint, ranking last in K% (26.1%); 29th in wRC+ (90) and average (.227); 28th in wOBA (.299); 27th in OPS (.681); and 24th in runs scored (341) from June 2 through Sept. 7.
Judge’s latest IL stint also comes with just 10 games remaining in the regular season. That was prior to beginning a three-game series at Arizona’s Chase Field on Friday. The second-place Yanks, who have already secured a playoff berth, will then host a highly-anticipated four-game series against the division-leading Rays from Sept. 22-24.
Now they’ll play those games without their best player, worsening the Bombers’ already-unlikely odds of snatching a division title from Tampa Bay.

item.content:encoded:
Aaron Judge Injured, Latest Updates on Yankees Star's Timeline to Return Ahead of 2026 MLB Playoffs
Just over a week after he returned from a rib injury that kept him out for most of the season, Aaron Judge is heading back to the injured list.
Judge is being placed on the 10-day IL with a calf strain, the New York Yankees announced Friday.
TOP NEWS
Mets 1B Has Memory Loss After Collision
Mets player calls out own fans
Ichiro Throws CRAZY Shutout 🔱
Judge left Wednesday's game against the Minnesota Twins in the sixth inning because of right lower leg tightness. He said after the game that he felt something during the first inning and eventually decided he should come out.
Judge went 0-for-2 with a pair of strikeouts before he exited the game. Heliot Ramos pinch-hit for him.
Judge suffered a rib injury in late May and missed more than three months of action, finally making his return last Tuesday against the Colorado Rockies. Since returning, he's gone 4-for-21 with a home run and three RBI, clearly still working his way back to 100 percent.
After his return, the three-time AL MVP addressed having to get back into shape while simultaneously helping the Yankees fight for ideal playoff seeding.
"I get paid to do this, so I gotta go do it," Judge told reporters. "That's the end of it. I get paid to go out there and give my best to the New York Yankees and these fans. So, you get paid to win games so you gotta keep going out there and winning games."
Luckily for Judge, New York managed to stay afloat during his absence. The Yankees are sitting in second place in the AL East and secured a spot in the postseason earlier this week.
The Bronx Bombers are six games ahead of the Boston Red Sox and should be able to secure the top wild-card spot.
Even though New York has guaranteed a spot in the playoffs, Judge's injury is worrisome. The Yankees may have managed when he was gone, but making a World Series push without their star would be a different story.
With Judge heading back to the injured list, the Yankees will hope their star slugger can return to the lineup sooner rather than later as New York battles for playoff position in the AL East.

item.dc:creator: Greg Kuffner; Unknown
item.description: The Cincinnati Reds claimed infielder and outfielder Oswaldo Cabrera off waivers from the New York Yankees on Friday, adding a versatile player who clearly made an impression on the people around him, as well as the fans. item.content:encoded:
The Cincinnati Reds claimed infielder and outfielder Oswaldo Cabrera off waivers from the New York Yankees on Friday, adding a versatile player who clearly made an impression on the people around him, as well as the fans.
The reaction from those who knew Cabrera in New York said plenty about the person Cincinnati is getting.
Jack Curry of the YES Network shared a strong endorsement of Cabrera after the move was announced.
“Oswaldo Cabrera, who is as kind and as gracious as any baseball player I’ve covered, is headed to the Reds. Best of luck to a versatile player and a gem of a human being.”
That is high praise from someone who has spent decades covering baseball. Curry’s comments were similar to the comments made by Yankees manager Aaron Boone.
“I’m blessed to have a lot of guys on this team that you just admire and respect and love doing the job with on a daily basis," Boone told the New York Daily News. "Oswaldo’s right there at the top of that list... The good thing is, Oswaldo’s come back from a very difficult injury and had a really good year down at Triple-A. He’s playing really well, so hopefully this is just one of those things. I’m confident that Oswaldo will go on to have a very good career, and hopefully it’s still with us.”
Boone’s hope of keeping Cabrera in the organization ultimately did not happen. Instead, the Reds will give him his next opportunity.
Cabrera Has Played Well in the Minors This Season
Cabrera has hit .232/.292/.343 across 304 career major league games. After missing most of 2025 with an injury, he appeared in just three major league games this season.
His production at Triple-A this season gives Reds fans something to be optimistic about. Cabrera hit .288/.345/.444 with 19 home runs in 122 games, putting together the kind of season Boone referenced while discussing his recovery.
Cabrera has played six different positions at Triple-A this season, appearing in 55 games at third base, 39 at shortstop, 12 at second base, 10 in left field, eight in right field and six at first base.
His ability to play both the infield and outfield gives the Reds options. He will still have to turn that Triple-A production into results at the major league level, but he arrives with strong support from people who watched him work every day.
Greg Kuffner a contributor to Reds On SI. He graduated from the University of Cincinnati and worked for the Sports Information Department during his time as a student. He follows all things Reds year round, including the minor league system.

item.title: [MLB.com] ¿Cómo responderán los jóvenes de Yankees en los playoffs?
item.dc:creator: Patrick Donnelly
item.description: Es común pensar en los Yankees como un equipo experimentado en los playoffs. Después de todo, ésta es la octava vez en nueve años que han llegado a la postemporada bajo la dirección del manager Aaron Boone. Y una rápida mirada a algunos de sus jugadores principales muestra una alineación que varía entre un poco y una gran cantidad de experiencia en octubre. item.content:encoded:
Es común pensar en los Yankees como un equipo experimentado en los playoffs. Después de todo, ésta es la octava vez en nueve años que han llegado a la postemporada bajo la dirección del manager Aaron Boone. Y una rápida mirada a algunos de sus jugadores principales muestra una alineación que varía entre un poco y una gran cantidad de experiencia en octubre.
Jugador, Número de Partidos de Playoffs de por vida
Cody Bellinger, 76
Aaron Judge, 65
Paul Goldschmidt, 29
Trent Grisham, 26
Jazz Chisholm, Jr. 24
Austin Wells, 21
Anthony Volpe, 21
Amed Rosario, 11
Ryan McMahon, 10
Ben Rice, 6
José Caballero, 3
Pero faltan algunos nombres en esa lista: El campocorto George Lombard Jr., el jardinero Spencer Jones, el primera base dominicano Luis García Jr. y el jardinero puertorriqueño Heliot Ramos. Ninguno de esos cuatro nunca ha jugado en la postemporada, ya sea con los Yankees o, como es el caso de García y Ramos, con sus equipos anteriores.
Ahora, es posible que algunos de los jugadores veteranos lesionados -- Grisham y Chisholm, específicamente -- puedan regresar a la alineación y enviar a algunos de esos nuevos rostros a la banca o fuera del roster de postemporada por completo. Pero es seguro decir que los Yankees van a contar con al menos algunos novatos en los playoffs el próximo mes, en su búsqueda de ganar su primera Serie Mundial desde el 2009.
Boone ha expresado que sus jóvenes y los recién llegados a los playoffs tienen otra ventaja sobre los jugadores en otros mercados.
"Jugar para los Yankees, jugar en Nueva York”, dijo, "tiene una manera de prepararte para la postemporada”.
Éste ha sido un año de transición en las Grandes Ligas. Consulta la primera ronda del Draft del 2023 si quieres pruebas. No menos de 19 de las 37 selecciones de primera ronda y de compensación han debutado en las Mayores, y muchos de ellos ya son jugadores clave en sus equipos.
"Los jugadores están llegando a las Grandes Ligas a un ritmo muy rápido ahora y a temprana edad”, manifestó el piloto de los Tigers, A.J. Hinch, quien ha dado la bienvenida a la tercera selección Max Clark y al favorito para Novato del Año de la Liga Americana, Kevin McGonigle, a Detroit este año. "No creo que se sientan tan impresionados por los grandes pasos que están dando”.
Para los Yankees, ese grupo incluye a Lombard, quien se ha aclimatado bien desde que fue subido a principios de agosto. Y Jones fue elogiado recientemente nada menos que por Aaron Judge, quien dijo que el jardinero novato "realmente ha evolucionado cada vez que ha sido subido, mejorando un poco más en cada ocasión”.
Por supuesto, habrá contratiempos en el camino. El miércoles, Jones se fue de 6-0 con cinco ponches y cometió un error cuando dejó caer un batazo en el jardín central. Y Lombard no pudo atrapar un roletazo del boricua Victor Caratini en la 13ª entrada que fue considerado un sencillo mientras los Mellizos vencían a los Yankees.
Pero cualquiera que siga el béisbol sabe que los días malos y las malas jugadas son parte del ciclo de crecimiento de un jugador de Grandes Ligas. La clave es aprender de ellos para poder limitarlos en el futuro. Y todo ello -- lo bueno, lo malo y lo ocasionalmente feo -- ayuda a preparar a un joven jugador para su primera vez jugando en el béisbol de octubre.
El mundo está a punto de descubrir lo preparados que están los Yankees jóvenes. Pero Jones ofreció un poco de tranquilidad el lunes mientras disfrutaba de la celebración en el vestuario después de la victoria en Target Field que aseguró otra clasificación de Nueva York para los playoffs.
"Creo que para nosotros, jugamos mejor cuando la multitud se vuelve más ruidosa", dijo. "Estoy bien emocionado por lo que está por venir”.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Yankees Announce Starting Pitchers for Diamondbacks Series: Gerrit Cole Must Get Back on Track
item.dc:creator: Joseph Randazzo; Unknown
item.description: If there's one reason to think the New York Yankees have a minuscule chance of overcoming a five-game deficit in the American League East, it's the probable pitchers every series. item.content:encoded:
If there's one reason to think the New York Yankees have a minuscule chance of overcoming a five-game deficit in the American League East, it's the probable pitchers every series. Aaron Boone's Bombers can feature one of his many frontline starters on a given night, and in this series against the Arizona Diamondbacks, two of his four best pitchers take the mound.
On paper, you see the first two starters and think the advantage should go to the Yankees, but one issue in particular has hampered their former Cy Young winner. If this team is going to make any noise in the postseason, he'll have to work on it, and it starts with this series.
Friday, Sept. 18 (9:40 p.m. ET): Gerrit Cole (NYY) vs. Eduardo Rodriguez (ARI)
Eduardo Rodriguez has proven to be a playoff-caliber pitcher, and his 2.62 ERA in 178.1 IP is frontline stuff. He is the type of high-level arm they'll see in the postseason. Rodriguez typically pitches to contact, holding opposing batters to an 87.3 MPH average exit velocity and a 33% hard-hit rate. This can be one of those games where the Yankees hit ground balls against him for 7+ innings.
Cole, meanwhile, has been snakebit by the long ball, and it isn't so wild to say that the advantage could go to Rodriguez in this one if Cole pitches the way he has. It's been a concerning turn of events ever since that game against the San Diego Padres. For now, the advantage goes to Rodriguez, who'll want to harken back to his Boston days and shut down the Yankees.
Saturday, Sept. 19 (8:10 p.m. ET): Cam Schlittler (NYY) vs. Brandon Pfadt (ARI)
Pfaadt, though, isn't a slouch by any means, and if the Yankees are going to be without Aaron Judge — which usually means the offense will be listless — what can be said about Rodriguez applies to Pfaadt here.
The 27-year-old Arizona starter has a 68th-percentile groundball rate and holds hitters to a 35.5% hard-hit rate. It could be another instance of the Yankees hitting a ton of ground balls. Most competent offenses should be able to hold their own, but it's hard to trust the Yankees 1-through-9 these days. They might need a great pitching performance by Schlittler and win one of those 2-0 or 3-0 games here.
Pfaadt has one of the best walk rates in baseball. His 5.7% BB% is in the 91st percentile, so he'll force them to make contact, and that can be a recipe for disaster for a team that can't put together runs.
Sunday, Sept. 20 (4:10 p.m. ET): Will Warren (NYY) vs. Corbin Burnes (ARI)
Corbin Burnes has pitched all of 7.2 innings this season. He's coming back from Tommy John surgery, which he had last June. It feels like a quick recovery, and he'll likely be on a pitch limit. That said, the sooner the Yankees can get him back in the game, the better.
Every Warren start can't be a high-scoring affair because he can be brilliant or a disaster, so hopefully they get a brilliant Warren here while also chasing Burnes out of the game quickly. If he's out by the third, they can ground down that bullpen.
Warren is coming off a solid outing against the Twins earlier this week, where he allowed five hits, two runs (zero earned), two walks, and racked up six strikeouts in 5.2 innings.
The advantage should go to the Yankees if Warren gives them length, but again, as with any game, it will come down to whether they can score.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.

item.dc:creator: Cole Shelton

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees could make a surprising decision on veteran infielder Ryan McMahon before the playoffs.
New York clinched a playoff berth. They will likely be in the Wild Card series again, likely playing the Boston Red Sox for the second year in a row.
The Yankees are 88-64.
New York Yankees Could Bench Ryan McMahon
With the Yankees heading back to the playoffs, New York could have to make a difficult decision on veteran infielder Ryan McMahon.
McMahon is a solid glove-first third baseman, but he has struggled offensively since coming to New York. With that, Yankees analyst Pat Ragazzo of FanSided believes New York could remove McMahon from its playoff roster, or simply have him on the bench.
"Should Rosario's hot streak continue into the end of the regular season, the Yankees find a way to utilize him at third base during the postseason," Ragazzo wrote. "There's even a world where Jose Caballero slides to third, with Anthony Volpe available off the bench. McMahon will probably still get a roster spot, but they cannot play his bat regularly in the biggest games of the year. McMahon's bat creates a black hole in the Yankees' lineup, which they cannot afford to deploy in October.
"If not for his defense, McMahon would've likely been designated for assignment by now. And given his historically poor offensive numbers, it seems like it could be headed that way with McMahon under contract for another year at $16 million. The 31-year-old just has not worked out as a member of the Yankees. His time in pinstripes should come to an end sooner rather than later."
McMahon has one more year on his six-year, $70 million deal. Not having him on the playoff roster would be a tough look. Yet, his bat has struggled, and the Yankees could use Caballero at third, with Volpe as the primary backup infielder in the playoffs.
McMahon is hitting .210 with 10 home runs and 34 RBIs this season.
New York Right Now
The Yankees have clinched a playoff spot and once again have World Series aspirations.
Although New York did clinch a playoff spot, the Yankees know the job is not done.
"Every year you go through a lot, it seems like. But we've been through a lot this year with injuries, with adversity," Yankees manager Aaron Boone said. "But credit to them for coming together. Through all the ups and downs, they've been a together group. I feel like they've developed a lot of grit over the season."
The Yankees are set to begin a three-game road series against the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday.
